items.title: Why the Fragile Trump-Xi Truce Could Break Before the U.S.-China D.C. Summit
items.summary: Chinese leader Xi Jinping and President Donald Trump are set to meet later this month in yet another bid to stabilize the relationship—and extend a truce struck last fall.  The planned Sept. 24 meeting in Washington, D.C., which Beijing has still yet to confirm, will mark Xi’s first trip to the capitol in more than a decade.  It follows Trump’s trip to Beijing last May, when the two dialed down tensions following months of tariff threats and, among other things, export restrictions.
